_readme: Project changelog + version ledger. `app_version` bumps on every Claude-assisted change; `strategy_versions` bump ONLY when an engine's tradeable parameters, gates or detectors change. lib/version.py is the read API; the engines stamp these onto every position, so a trade can always be traced back to the code that opened it. Entries are newest-first. Entries with source='reconstructed' were rebuilt from session notes on 2026-08-21 (before the ledger existed) and their exact dates are best-effort; source='live' entries were written at the time of the change.

signals.note: Original strict-pullback entry: down 2 days + bottom 20% of 5d range + RSI<35 + ret_20d>-15%. Retired as -EV (needs 80% WR, delivers ~60%).
Switched to the backtest-validated mean-reversion setup: DoD <= -1%, no-Friday, not-at-5d-high. Break-even WR 33.3%.
SL widened -1.0% -> -2.0% to survive opening volatility. Never re-backtested; moved break-even WR 33.3% -> 50.0%.

SL cooldown cut 7d -> 1d (same-day block only). CORRECTED 2026-08-24: this row previously also claimed a pattern-confluence entry gate. live_signals.py has never contained one — `git log --all -S confluence -- live_signals.py` is empty across every commit. CONFLUENCE_REQUIRED exists only in live_patterns.py (added in 51acb24); requiring a Patterns fire alongside a Signals candidate is live_cross's entire job, not something Signals ever did. The claim came from the 2026-08-21 ledger reconstruction conflating the engines.

signals.params: TP +2.0% / SL -2.0% / 7d hold, cooldown 1d, STALE guard
signals.note: Close-settle gate fixed (5-min tolerance) restoring the EOD sweep, and positions >4d past target now book STALE at market instead of a synthetic TP/SL fill. CORRECTED 2026-08-24: 'confluence required' removed from params — see sig-4.

signals.params: TP +2.0% / SL -2.0% / 7d hold, cooldown 1d, STALE guard, AUTO-ENTRY at ask, no entry after 16:30
signals.note: Primary signals auto-enter at ask again, reverting the 2026-05-27 manual-only flow under which the wallet held zero open positions. Added a 16:30 late-entry cutoff to match patterns/cross — the manual flow never needed one because good-for-the-day limit orders expired at the close. Entry filter itself (DoD <= -1%, not-at-5d-high, no-Friday, ret_20d > -15%) and TP/SL/hold are unchanged; what changed is that clearing the filter now buys instead of surfacing.

signals.params: TP +2.0% / SL -1.0% / 7d hold, cooldown 1d, STALE guard, AUTO-ENTRY at ask, no entry after 16:30
signals.note: Stop restored -2.0% -> -1.0%, back to the backtested pair (40.9% WR, +72 SEK/trade, profitable 10 of 11 years). The -2.0% stop ran from 2026-05-25, was widened to survive opening volatility, was never re-backtested, and moved break-even WR from 33.3% to 50.0%; the engine delivered 43.8% (7W/9L over 16 scored) and -388 SEK/trade against it. Signals only — Patterns (pat-3) and Cross (x-2) still run -2.0%, which keeps Patterns as a control group on the same TP/hold with different entry logic.

signals.params: TP +2.0% / SL -1.0% / 7d hold, cooldown 1d, STALE guard, AUTO-ENTRY at ask, no entry after 16:30, liquidity cap 5% of median daily volume, cross-wallet stem dedupe
signals.note: Two new entry gates. Liquidity: a position may not exceed 5% of the name's median daily volume (from ohlc/), falling back to today's cumulative volume when no history exists; 13 of the 158-name universe now fail it, all A/D-class or genuinely thin listings. Cross-wallet dedupe: a company stem held in the Patterns or Cross wallet is no longer buyable here.

signals.params: TP +2.0% / SL -1.0% / 7d hold, cooldown 1d, STALE guard, CLOSE-CONFIRMED ENTRY (one post-close pass, filled at the official close), liquidity cap 5% of median daily volume, cross-wallet stem dedupe
signals.note: Entries move off the intraday tick and onto the confirmed close. Measured by replaying this exact filter over 64 entry days of minute data (2026-04-30..2026-08-20), varying only the execution regime: close entry + close exit n=2346 46.6% WR +0.372%/trade; close entry + intraday exit n=2346 43.5% WR +0.301%; intraday entry + intraday exit (sig-8) n=4352 40.2% WR +0.202%. Entering intraday nearly doubles the trade count by taking names that dip 1% and recover before the close - trades the backtest never saw - and costs ~45% of the per-trade edge. Chosen because the wallet is slot-constrained rather than signal-constrained (6 open against a 35k floor), so per-trade quality outranks signal count. NOT a fix for the sig-8 result: at 7W/16L against a true 40.2%, P(<=7 wins in 23) = 23%, i.e. ordinary variance - roughly 200 trades are needed before the win rate separates from the 33.3% break-even at all. Carries a mild lookahead (the close both triggers the entry and sets the fill), the same assumption the arm-B figure was measured under; the real-world equivalent is a closing-auction order.

patterns.note: Engine launched. Bullish Engulfing, Morning Star, Piercing Line, Three White Soldiers, Tweezer Bottom, Hammer on intraday-aggregated daily bars.

patterns.params: TP +2.0% / SL -2.0% / 7d hold, 6 bullish patterns, Hammer parity fixes
patterns.note: Hammer detector tightened: bull-body gate, doji floor, 1.5% downtrend floor. Dry-run vetoed 5/6 historical losers while preserving the Telia winner.

patterns.params: TP +2.0% / SL -2.0% / 7d hold, 5 entry-eligible patterns, STALE guard
patterns.note: Hammer moved to detect-only (ENTRY_DISABLED_PATTERNS) after -6,637 SEK, and the shared STALE exit guard applied.

patterns.params: TP +2.0% / SL -2.0% / 7d hold, 5 entry-eligible patterns, STALE guard, liquidity cap 5% of median daily volume, cross-wallet stem dedupe
patterns.note: Same two gates as sig-8. Motivated by this engine's 2026-08-24 Electrolux A fill: 2,380 shares against a 4,460-share day, 53% of all volume, on a quote that never moved off the fill price.

cross.params: TP +2.0% / SL -2.0% / 7d hold, Signals radar AND fresh Patterns fire
cross.note: Engine launched. Confluence-only wallet, user approves every entry; consumes recent_pattern_fires rather than detecting.

cross.params: entries paused, exits still managed, STALE guard
cross.note: Entries paused after the wallet inverted Patterns' edge (-9,570 SEK, 37.5% WR). Exits, candidate computation and reporting continue.

cross.params: entries paused, exits still managed, STALE guard, liquidity cap 5% of median daily volume, cross-wallet stem dedupe
cross.note: Same two gates as sig-8, surfaced in each candidate's skip_reasons so the Approve control renders disabled. Bites hardest here: every Cross candidate is by construction a name both upstream engines like, so it is above-average likely to already be held by one of them.

entries.title: Close-confirmed entry for Signals, and a sector tag on every stock
entries.summary: Signals stops buying on the first intraday tick that dips 1% and instead fills once per day at the confirmed close (sig-9). Separately, stock_names.csv gains a sector column so a correlated book is visible in the log and on the page - informational only, nothing gates on it.
changes: live_signals.py: ENTRY_AT_CLOSE + close_confirmed_entry_ready(). The post-close launchd tick now falls THROUGH into the ordinary scan instead of returning, so entries run once per day against closing prices. Gated on last_ohlc_capture_date rather than a wall-clock window - capture only stamps that date after probe_data_lag() shows the feed past 17:30, and it fires on any post-close tick. A fixed 17:20-17:30 window was rejected: on 2026-08-31 zero runs landed in it (Mac asleep 16:12-18:04), so that design would have skipped the day's entries silently.

live_signals.py: the pass fills at the confirmed close, not the ask. Caught in the first dry run - BONESUPPORT filled at its 220.20 ask against a 218.60 close, booking an instant -0.73% that the arm-B measurement never assumed. Intraday keeps the ask, which is a real executable offer. fill_type now records 'close' vs 'auto'.

live_signals.py: an intraday run no longer buys at all; candidates surface as pending ('awaiting close confirmation') so the page still shows what is building during the session. last_entry_scan_date makes the pass once-per-day and is stamped at the very end, so a crash midway retries the whole pass rather than losing the day. entry_gate persists {open, reason} every run - a day with no entries always says why instead of looking like 'no signals'.

stock_names.csv: appended columns 4 (sector_id) and 5 (sector_name), backfilled for all 58,976 rows by scripts/tag_sectors.py. 1,980 rows carry a sector; the 158-name tradable universe is at 100% coverage. Uses the feed's numeric sector/sectorname pair, NOT sectorl3name - L3 splits Fabege ('Kommersiella Fastigheter'), Wihlborgs ('Kontor') and Pandox ('Hotell & Resort') into three unrelated-looking sectors, while sectorname puts all three in 'Fastigheter'.

live_signals.py + app.py: the cap tier is now read from row[3], never row[-1]. Both read the LAST column, so appending sector columns would have matched a sector name against the tier whitelist and silently emptied the universe for all three engines (build_universe is shared via live_patterns/live_cross).

lib/webScrapper.py: _read_names_csv/_write_names_csv/_merge_name carry the sector columns through, so an ordinary refresh sweep cannot wipe them; new upsert_sectors_bulk() writes only columns 4-5 and ignores insrefs not already in the file.

lib/webScrapper.py: _write_names_csv no longer swallows write failures. It printed nothing and returned normally on error, so callers reported success ('1,980 written') against an unchanged file - indistinguishable from a working write until something much later read the columns back and found them gone.
lib/engine_common.py: sector_map() (mtime-cached, keyed by display name, mirrors app._live_tier_map) and sector_concentration() grouping positions by sector with SEK exposure.
app.py: /live-sectors serves the map, mirroring /live-tiers.

web: Sector column and concentration bars under Open positions on /live-signals; sectorPill/sectorConcentration in live_common.js mirror the Python helper so page and log agree; .sector-pill and .conc-* tokens in style.css. The sector pill is not uppercased - the names are full Swedish phrases that turn into an unreadable block at 10px.
entries.notes: Trigger: on 2026-08-31, 16 of the 17 real-estate names in the universe fell together (mean -1.71% against -0.63% for everything else) and four of the day's six exits were property, 4,199 of the 5,586 SEK lost. Nothing in the project stored a sector - sectorl3name was fetched per-quote for the web UI and discarded, and the scraper's 'Instrumenttype/Classification Sector/' tree is empty. The tag is deliberately informational: across all 151 closed trades real estate is the BEST segment (17 trades, 52.9% WR, +137/trade) against everything else (134 trades, 46.3% WR, -110/trade), so a concentration cap would be cutting into the strongest sample on the book. Decide that on evidence the tag now makes it possible to collect. Also note the changeover guard: last_entry_scan_date was stamped to 2026-08-31 by hand so the new pass could not retroactively re-trade a day already traded intraday under sig-8. REQUIRES AN app.py RESTART - the long-running server holds the pre-change 4-column CSV writer and its 60s refresh thread wipes the sector columns until it is restarted.

entries.title: Live Signals page adopts the section-card layout used by Patterns
entries.summary: The Signals page was the last live page still drawing bare .section-title headings above flat .table-wrap boxes with its own hard-coded palette. Every block is now a .section card — title, subtitle and table inside one bordered surface — styled from the style.css tokens, so Signals, Patterns and Cross read as one app.
changes: web/live_signals.html: replaced .table-wrap (10px radius, no header inside) with the shared .section card (--radius-lg, 18px 22px padding, 18px gap) that live_patterns.html and live_cross.html already use. Each section-title and its explanatory paragraph moved inside the card; .approved-summary was dropped in favour of the shared .section-subtitle, and the long '— approve to trade' style suffixes are now .panel-note spans, matching Patterns' 'Blocked this run' heading.

Palette: every hard-coded hex in the page's <style> block (#f0f3fa, #1a1f36, #8a94a6, #e8ecf5, #0052cc, #1a8042, #b32a36 …) now reads from the :root tokens. The approve button and the limit-price input adopt live_cross.html's token-based definitions. Only the deep-pullback purple (#f3effe/#7a4dcc), which has no token, stays literal.

Analytics: .equity-card and the four .analytics-panel boxes became .section cards, their .panel-title became .section-title, and their bare <table>s became .sig-table so the breakdowns match the 'By version' table on the Patterns page. .analytics-grid now only controls the 2-up layout and uses align-items:start so the short 'By conviction' card no longer stretches to the height of 'By ticker'. The floating 'Equity curve' and 'Performance breakdown' headings are gone — the titles live inside the cards they label, which also fixes the orphaned headings that stayed on screen while renderAnalytics() hid their content on a wallet with no closed trades.

The Run now / market / lag / SPX toolbar and the Latest run log are card-wrapped too, and the pagination footers moved inside their table's card (with flex-wrap so a narrow card wraps them instead of widening the page).
Tables are now inside .section, so style.css's mobile rule that makes '.section table' horizontally scrollable finally applies to this page — .table-wrap was never in that selector list.
entries.notes: Presentation only: no strategy bump, no engine or endpoint change, and no JavaScript was touched. Every element id the page's render functions look up (equity-card, analytics-grid, approved-summary, forced-summary, cooldown-summary, the pager ids) is unchanged; only #cooldown-wrap was removed, and nothing referenced it. Note that feedback-page-design-standard names live_signals.html as the canonical visual reference — after this change the canonical example of a content section is the .section card as built on live_patterns.html.

entries.title: Liquidity gate, cross-wallet dedupe, and a stop-retighten tool
entries.summary: Three fixes from the 2026-08-24 trade audit: positions can no longer exceed 5% of a name's median daily volume, a company held in one wallet is no longer buyable in another, and a script brings already-open positions onto their engine's current SL_PCT without booking synthetic fills.
changes: lib/engine_common.py: new liquidity layer. median_daily_volume() reads ohlc/{insref}_OHLC.csv, counting only bars with volume > 0 (the 2026-06-13 backfill wrote volume=0 for all ~4,700 of its bars) and taking the median, not the mean, so one block trade cannot certify a dead ticker as liquid — Electrolux A printed 463,867 shares on 2026-08-19 against a ~4,000-share norm. liquidity_verdict() converts that into a SEK cap at MAX_PARTICIPATION = 5%; apply_liquidity_cap() folds it into each engine's own size cap so a mid-liquidity name takes a smaller position rather than being rejected outright.

Threshold evidence: 5% clears every entry the three engines have ever taken with 3.7x headroom (worst genuine trade is Atrium Ljungberg B at 1.34% of its median day on 2026-08-24) while rejecting the Electrolux A fill at 60.3%. Across the 158-name universe it blocks 13 and caps zero: Corem A, Tele2 A, Electrolux A, Sweco A, Stora Enso A, NCC A, Kinnevik A, Arion Bank SDB, Sagax A, Husqvarna A, Fenix Outdoor B, Tieto, Fastpartner D.

Fallback for the 240-name watchlist, which has no captured OHLC history: the quote's `quantity` field is the day's cumulative share volume (verified against the EOD capture — Electrolux B quantity=2,738,744 equals its 2026-08-24 OHLC volume), and the cap becomes 100% of it rather than 5%, because intraday volume is a partial day and 5% of it at 09:30 would reject the entire universe. 'You may not buy more shares than have traded all session' is weaker but true at any hour, and still stops the Electrolux A case. live_signals.get_live() now carries `quantity`; it was already in infoScrapper's _QUOTE_FIELDS, so this costs no extra API call.

No volume data at all leaves cap_sek = None and the engines must not block — treating absence as illiquidity would silently halt half of Signals, which is the failure shape this project keeps hitting.

lib/engine_common.py: foreign_held_stems() + sibling_wallets() give each engine a view of the other two books, collapsed to the company stem. 2026-08-24 closed with Electrolux B in Signals and Electrolux A in Patterns (140k of one company) and Securitas B in both Patterns and Cross. Signals had already rejected Electrolux A itself as a "duplicate of held 'Electrolux'" — it simply could not see the other wallets. Fails soft: an unreadable sibling contributes nothing rather than raising.

Wired into all three engines behind a per-engine CROSS_WALLET_DEDUPE flag, including live_signals' limit-order fill path (a resting order on a stem another wallet has since bought is cancelled). live_cross puts both gates into each candidate's skip_reasons so the Approve button renders disabled rather than enabled-and-lying.

web/live_patterns.html: new 'Blocked this run' panel, fed by new state["last_skipped"] and state["last_entry_gate"]. This engine's gate decisions previously existed only in logs/live_patterns.log — the page rendered a healthy wallet while the engine rejected every fire. Both fields are written inside _persist_ui_snapshot(), not at the entry stage, because the Friday and post-16:30 branches never reach that stage: leaving the list alone there would republish the previous run's rejections under a fresh last_run, the same stale-behind-a-fresh-timestamp trap that hid frozen prices on this page for weeks. last_entry_gate names the engine-level reason, so an empty list can never be misread as 'every fire was actionable'.

scripts/retighten_stops.py: brings already-open positions onto their engine's current SL_PCT. Dry-run by default, backs up to state/backups/ before writing, and refuses to write while an engine run is in flight (write_json_atomic prevents torn writes, not lost updates). Holds no parameters of its own — each target comes from the engine module's own SL_PCT, so it only acts where a wallet has drifted from the code it runs under.

live_signals.apply_exit_checks: a stop retightened below where the market already sits would fill at the stop price on the next run — a better-than-market exit that never existed, the same synthetic-fill problem STALE_EXIT_GRACE_DAYS was added to avoid. Positions marked sl_fill_at_market fill at the real market price instead, and the marker clears itself as soon as the position trades back above the new stop. So the tool never forces an exit: it sets the correct stop and lets the next session decide.

strategy_bumps.why: Two new entry gates: 5%-of-median-volume liquidity cap and cross-wallet stem dedupe. TP, SL and hold period unchanged.
Same two entry gates. TP, SL, hold period and the pattern set are unchanged.
Same two entry gates, surfaced in candidate skip_reasons. Entries remain paused.

entries.notes: The cross-wallet dedupe deliberately couples the three wallets: a Patterns entry now depends on what Signals happens to hold, so they are no longer independent strategy samples and the A/B comparison they were built for is weakened. Accepted because the aggregate book is one pot of money; CROSS_WALLET_DEDUPE = False in any engine restores independence. Separately, OHLC capture still covers only the large-cap universe, so the 240-name watchlist relies on the weaker intraday fallback until capture is extended.

entries.title: Signals stop restored to the backtested -1.0%
entries.summary: Reverts the un-backtested 2026-05-25 stop widening, taking break-even WR from 50.0% back to 33.3% on Live Signals only.
changes: live_signals.py SL_PCT -0.020 -> -0.010. TP, hold period and every entry gate are unchanged.

Evidence: 20 closed trades, 4 excluded as outage STALEs. Of the 16 scored, 7W/9L = 43.8% WR and -388 SEK/trade against a 50.0% break-even. Six of the seven wins were MANUAL clips at +0.80%..+1.69% (avg +1.18%); the +2% TP fired once in twenty. Naive replay of the 9 stops at -1% instead of -2% turns -6,215 into +77 — an upper bound, since a tighter stop also stops out trades that later recovered into a clip.

web/live_common.js: BREAKEVEN_WR is no longer one shared constant. New setBreakeven(tp, sl) computes |SL|/(TP+|SL|) and each live page declares its own engine's pair, so Signals' win-rate tile scores against 33% while Patterns and Cross keep scoring against 50%. The 0.50 default is the -2.0% case, so a page that forgets to call it gets the stricter bar rather than a flattering one.
Subtitle, help.html strategy rules and the engine docstring all updated; help.html states explicitly that the change is Signals-only.

strategy_bumps.why: Stop-loss moved -2.0% -> -1.0%, halving risk per trade and moving break-even WR from 50.0% to 33.3%.

entries.notes: Scope was a deliberate choice: Patterns and Cross stay at -2.0% so Patterns remains a control group running the same TP and hold on different entry logic. The 7 positions Signals opened earlier today under sig-6 were LEFT at their original -2.0% stops rather than retightened — they are the wallet of record and were opened under a different contract. All 7 are currently between -0.14% and 0.00%, so none is past a -1% stop; retightening them is still available as a clean one-shot if that is preferred. Expect a higher stop-out rate than the last three months: that is the trade the backtest says is worth making, and it is the thing to watch rather than be surprised by.

entries.title: Ledger correction — Signals never had a confluence entry gate
entries.summary: sig-4 and sig-5 documented an entry gate that has never existed in live_signals.py; the params and notes now match the code.
changes: sig-4 params: dropped 'confluence required'; note rewritten to record the correction and the evidence.
sig-5 params: dropped 'confluence required'.

Verified exhaustively rather than by inspection: `git log --all -S confluence -- live_signals.py` returns no commits, and grepping live_signals.py at 5138cfa / 51acb24 / d7c9511 / 0dc8ad0 finds zero hits. The only occurrences of the string anywhere in history are live_patterns.py, live_cross.py, and CHANGELOG.json itself.

Root cause: both rows were written by the 2026-08-21 ledger reconstruction (source='reconstructed'), which attributed the 2026-06-13 Patterns confluence gate to Signals because the two changes share a date.
entries.notes: No code change and no strategy bump — the code was always right, the documentation was wrong. Worth noting the blast radius while it stood: sig-4 and sig-5 cover 6 closed trades whose exit stats would have been read as 'confluence-gated' when they were nothing of the kind. Reconstructed rows predating 2026-08-21 should be treated as claims to verify, not as record.

entries.title: Signals auto-enters again; Patterns wallet topped up to 1M
entries.summary: Reverts Signals to automatic entry at ask like Patterns, and adds 500k to the Patterns wallet with deposit-aware return accounting.
changes: live_signals.py: a candidate clearing every gate is now bought at ask on the run that finds it (fill_type='auto'), instead of being surfaced as pending for the user to approve with a limit price. Same gates as before — stem-dedup, calendar event window, SL cooldown, cash floor — and sizing still comes from CONVICTION_SIZING.

Added LATE_ENTRY_CUTOFF_MIN (16:30 local) to live_signals, matching patterns/cross. The manual flow never needed one: orders were good-for-the-day and expired at the close. Auto-entry without it would buy into the closing auction.

pending_signals now means 'cleared every gate but was not bought' — below the 35k floor after rounding, or past the 16:30 cutoff — with a not_taken reason. The approve + buy-limit machinery is untouched and still fills those by hand.

Watchlist and near-miss approvals are unchanged as gates: an unapproved mid/small cap still never reaches the candidate list (order size can exceed available volume). Once approved it now buys at market rather than waiting for a user-set limit, and the approval is consumed as before.

engine_common.wallet_start(state, default) + a wallet_start field on all three wallets: return% is measured against contributed capital, so a deposit does not read as profit. deposits[] in the same state file is the audit trail.

Patterns wallet: +500,000 SEK deposit (cash 12,876 -> 512,876, contributed 500k -> 1M). It was fully deployed — 12,876 SEK against a 35,000 SEK position floor — so no pattern fire could be taken. Equity 1,006,608 reads +0.66% rather than the +101% a naive top-up would have shown.
UI: all six hardcoded baselines (three engine pages, the overview's 1,500k, the per-engine cards' 500k, and live_widget.js) now read wallet_start and sum the real per-engine figures.

strategy_bumps.why: Entry gate changed: clearing the filter now opens a position at ask instead of surfacing a candidate, plus a new 16:30 late-entry cutoff.

entries.notes: The LaunchAgent fired at 13:04 local while this change was being finished and Signals immediately opened 7 positions (~70k each), taking cash from 488,189 to 2 SEK — the whole wallet deployed in one run, which is what auto-entry with a 70k target against 7 qualifying large caps does. Those 7 were stamped sig-5 / 0.12.0 because the ledger had not been updated yet; they have been corrected to sig-6 / 0.13.0 so the version grouping matches the code that opened them. Worth knowing before reading the next win-rate roll-up: Signals was -EV over its 20 closed trades (-11,811 SEK realized) under the manual flow, and every historical win came from a manual clip at +0.8-1.7% rather than the +2% TP ever firing. Separately, sig-4/sig-5's params string claims a 'confluence required' entry gate that does not exist anywhere in live_signals.py — CONFLUENCE_REQUIRED lives only in live_patterns.py. Not introduced here, but the ledger overstates what Signals enforces.

entries.title: Index-range scrape runs at the configured worker count
entries.summary: Both scrape phases now scale off the refresh_workers setting instead of a hardcoded 8 and a sequential loop — roughly 7h04m to 3h10m on a full-range run.
changes: run_search() takes a `workers` argument (clamped 1..16, mirroring app.MAX_REFRESH_WORKERS since both phases hit the same intradaychart endpoint that plateau was measured on); app.py passes _refresh_worker_count() so the scrape scales off the same Settings knob as Update All.

Phase 1 (index probe) thread count is no longer hardcoded at 8. Measured on the real endpoint: 123 idx/s at 8 threads vs 229 idx/s at 16, a 1.86x speedup. This phase is ~79% of a full-range run's wall clock, so it is what actually decides scrape duration.
Phase 3 (price scrape) was a fully sequential loop at ~103 ms per stock; now a ThreadPoolExecutor over the same worker count. Stubbed 60-stock benchmark: 6.22s at 1 worker, 0.83s at 8, 0.43s at 16.

Fixed out-of-range probing in the static chunking: with more threads than indices, surplus threads got ranges starting past end_index and the ones in between probed indices outside the requested range (a request for 5-7 actually probed 5 through 11 at the old 8 threads). num_threads is now capped at the span; verified across seven edge cases.
status['checked'] += 1 was an unlocked read-modify-write across every probe thread, so the progress bar undercounted; now under _counter_lock along with the phase 3 counters.
Settings copy updated — the worker count now covers scrapes too, not just Update All.
entries.notes: Not done, deliberately: urlcheck and fetch_stock build a byte-identical URL, so phase 1 downloads a ~198 KB payload, keeps only the header, and phase 3 re-downloads the same bytes — about 10 GB fetched twice on a full run. Reusing them needs phases 1-3 collapsed into one write-as-you-discover pass (buffering rows for ~52k stocks would want ~10 GB of RAM), which changes the progress UI's phase model, the early-stop semantics, and writes prices that are hours stale by the end of a long run. Also measured and rejected: a lighter cmd=quote probe for phase 1 — 73 ms vs 136 ms on a hit but 86 ms vs 74 ms on a miss, and ~98.5% of a 3.5M sweep is misses, so it is latency-bound, not payload-bound. Still outstanding from the same review: run_search ignores update_filter, replaces stock_index.json instead of merging, never clears _dashboard_cache, and Stop does not interrupt phase 3.

entries.title: Patterns page showed frozen prices on Fridays and after 16:30
entries.summary: live_patterns.py's two early-return branches stamped a new last_run without refreshing last_quotes, so /live-patterns polled fresh-looking JSON and redrew stale prices.
changes: The Friday weekend-risk and post-16:30 cutoff branches called save_state() but returned before the build_quote_snapshot() block at the bottom of main(), so last_run advanced while last_quotes stayed frozen at the last full run's values. Open positions showed stale Current prices all day every Friday and every evening after 16:30 — roughly a third of market hours.

Snapshot hoisted into _persist_ui_snapshot(state, live, primary=()) and called on all three exit paths; primary defaults empty because the early-return paths have not scanned a universe, and open positions still resolve their ticker_paths from insref.

Diagnosed from an orphan last_quotes key: a ticker closed on TP at 10:29 was still in the snapshot hours later, which is only possible if the map had not been rebuilt since before it exited. The engine log carried the correct live prices the whole time.
live_signals.py and live_cross.py checked and unaffected — signals has no early return before its snapshot, and cross's market-closed branch skips save_state() entirely, so its last_run stays honest.
recent_pattern_fires deliberately left untouched on those paths: no scan ran, and live_cross ages fires out itself via PATTERN_FIRE_FRESH_HOURS.
entries.notes: No strategy bump — last_quotes and ticker_paths are UI-only. apply_exit_checks reads the in-memory `live` map, so TP/SL evaluation was always using correct prices; only the page was wrong. Fourth incident of the same shape: a gate fired, the log said so, the page kept rendering. Corollary worth generalising — a fresh last_run is not proof of fresh data.

entries.title: Changelog page + two-tier version tracking
entries.summary: Adds this ledger, a /changelog page, and stamps an app + strategy version onto every trade the three engines open.
changes: CHANGELOG.json — the ledger: app version, per-engine strategy versions, full strategy history, and one entry per change.
lib/version.py — read API over the ledger (mtime-cached), used by the engines to stamp and by app.py to serve.
All 3 engines stamp app_version + strategy_version onto each new position; apply_exit_checks carries them into closed_trades.
Backfilled strategy versions onto existing closed trades from strategy_history dates, flagged version_source='backfilled'.
/changelog page + /changelog-data endpoint; version pill on open + closed trade rows and a 'By version' panel on all 3 live pages.
Stop hook warns when code files change without a CHANGELOG.json entry.

First read of the backfilled record: pat-3 (Hammer entry-disabled) is running 83% WR / +0.88% avg / +3,697 SEK over 6 closed trades against pat-2's 39% / -0.34% / -3,762 — small n, but the first evidence the 2026-08-18 Hammer disable worked. Also isolates the outage damage: 4 of sig-4's 6 closed trades are STALE.
files: (nav link only) web/browse.html, dashboard.html, index.html, help.html, live_overview.html, ohlc_capture.html, settings.html, stock_template.html, stocksearch.html
entries.notes: Version stamping fails soft by design — a missing or half-written CHANGELOG.json yields an empty stamp and the engines trade on unaffected. Never let a docs file gate a trade.

entries.title: Cross pause surfaced in the UI
entries.summary: ENTRIES_PAUSED was invisible to the page, so 15 approvals silently queued against a paused engine.
changes: Pause now appends to each candidate's skip_reasons so Approve renders disabled.
entries_paused / paused_since / paused_reason persisted into state; amber notice on live_cross.html.
Queued-approval tooltip corrected — it had promised the engine would buy on the next run.

entries.title: Refresh performance overhaul
entries.summary: Parallel sweep, bulk name upserts and incremental history pulls.
changes: Parallel ThreadPoolExecutor sweep behind a refresh_workers setting (max 16).
upsert_names_bulk replaces the per-stock 2 MB stock_names.csv rewrite.
sync_history does incremental pulls with re-adjustment detection.
Startup sweep honours update_filter; run_search no longer truncates stock_names.csv to 2 columns.

entries.title: P0-P4 fixes — close-gate bug, health banner, STALE guard, Hammer off, Cross paused
entries.summary: A 6-second close-gate bug had silently killed the OHLC capture and EOD sweep for two months.
changes: P0: feed_settled_past_close demanded a trade at >= 17:30:00, but the closing auction prints at 17:29:54 — blocked both subsystems from 2026-06-13 to 2026-08-18. Fixed with CLOSE_SETTLE_TOLERANCE = 5 min.
P1: _live_health + /live-health endpoint and a health banner on every live page, measured against the last completed session.
P2: STALE_EXIT_GRACE_DAYS = 4 in the shared apply_exit_checks; 9 outage trades relabelled, P&L left untouched so cash reconciles.
P2: one BREAKEVEN_WR = 0.50 replaces three different hard-coded thresholds, two of them stale.
P3: Hammer entry-disabled but still detected.
P4: Cross entries paused.

strategy_bumps.reason: Close-settle gate fix + STALE exit guard

entries.title: Shared engine layer + widgets refactor (commit 51acb24)
entries.summary: Consolidated the three engines' duplicated helpers and grew the universe to the full Nordic name list.
changes: lib/engine_common.py — shared state I/O (atomic writes), local-clock date, entry gates, sizing, log rotation.
web/live_widget.js floating summary widget; lib/tradesScrapper.py.
stock_names.csv grown to the full ~59k Nordic universe.
New /calendar, /trades and live-cross endpoints.

entries.title: Live Cross launch, Hammer parity, OHLC trigger rewrite, 5-feature batch
entries.summary: Biggest single day of change — a third wallet, a detector fix, and the OHLC capture trigger finally firing.
changes: Live Cross engine launched: third paper wallet at /live-cross, user-approves confluence entries.
Hammer detector parity fixes: bull-body gate, doji floor, 1.5% downtrend floor.
OHLC capture trigger rewritten — maybe_capture_eod_ohlc + LaunchAgent StartCalendarInterval Mon-Fri 17:50 + pmset wakepoweron. Backfill seeded 4,724 bars.
TP-fire diagnostic: not a bug — the user clips manually at +0.75% before TP fires.
SL-cooldown visibility, pattern confluence gate (CONFLUENCE_REQUIRED = True), and the /live Overview tab with an SVG equity curve summing all 3 wallets.
SL cooldown reduced 7d -> same-day block only.

entries.title: Calendar event cache + filter smoke test
entries.summary: 6-month large-cap backtest: a +/-7d calendar filter lifts WR 2.7pp and avg return 11bp.
changes: lib/calendar_cache.py + state/events_calendar.json.
Smoke test validated the strategy at +0.49%/trade baseline; filter strongest in earnings season.
Volvo / Lundin / Autoliv flagged as over-blocked — asymmetric window candidate.

entries.title: Project folder reorganisation
entries.summary: Entry points at root, support modules in lib/, web assets in web/, runtime state in state/, logs in logs/.
changes: Support modules moved under lib/; new entry points must inject lib/ into sys.path.
Runtime state files moved to state/ and untracked.

entries.title: Live Patterns engine + stop widened to -2%
entries.summary: Second wallet launched, and the stop was widened to survive opening volatility — the single most consequential change in the project's history.
changes: live_patterns.py launched: candlestick-pattern entries on intraday-aggregated daily bars, separate 500k SEK wallet at /live-patterns.
SL widened -1.0% -> -2.0% across all engines. Never re-backtested. Break-even WR moved 33.3% -> 50.0%, which the 2026-08-18 review identified as the root cause of all three wallets being -EV.
OHLC capture under ohlc/ started (trigger was broken until 2026-06-13 — captured 0 bars).

entries.title: Switch to the validated +2/-1/7d strategy
entries.summary: The deployed 0.5%/-2%/5d pullback strategy was confirmed -EV in backtest and retired.
changes: 12- and 18-month backtests: 0.5% TP needs 80% WR, entry filter delivers ~60%. -0.36% to -0.44% per trade.
OMXS30 smoketest same day: 4,678 LIVE trades = -0.29% EV/trade vs 12,262 VALIDATED trades = +0.28%.
Engine switched to TP +2.0% / SL -1.0% / 7d hold, DoD <= -1%, no-Friday, not-at-5d-high.

entries.title: Live Signals paper-trade engine
entries.summary: First paper-trade wallet: 500k SEK, mean-reversion entries, 15-min LaunchAgent cadence.
changes: live_signals.py with a 500k SEK paper wallet at /live-signals.
Strict-pullback entry: down 2 days + bottom 20% of 5d range + RSI<35 + ret_20d>-15%. TP +0.5% / SL -2.0% / 5d hold.
